questions.q: What does the psalmist declare about Yahweh?
questions.a: The psalmist declares that Yahweh reigns and calls for everyone on earth to rejoice and be glad.

questions.q: What is the foundation of Yahweh’s throne?
questions.a: The foundation of Yahweh’s throne is righteousness and justice.

questions.q: What is the result of the fire that goes before Yahweh?
questions.a: The fire that goes before Yahweh burns all of his enemies.
Yahweh’s lightning lights up the world, people on the earth see it, and it causes them to be afraid.

questions.q: What declares Yahweh’s righteousness and glory?
questions.a: Everything that people can see in the heavens makes it clear that he is righteous and all the people groups see how glorious he is.

questions.q: Who will be shamed by Yahweh?
questions.a: All those who worship carved images and are proud of their useless idols should be shamed by Yahweh.

questions.q: Why did Zion hear and the daughters of Judah rejoice?
questions.a: All the people of Jerusalem and all of Judah rejoiced because Yahweh judges people justly.

questions.q: What does the psalmist say about Yahweh?
questions.a: The psalmist says that Yahweh is the supreme king who rules over all the earth and more powerful than all other spirit beings.

questions.q: What does Yahweh do for his faithful?
questions.a: Yahweh protects the lives of his faithful ones and rescues them from the wicked.

questions.q: What does the psalmist say Yahweh provides for righteous people?
questions.a: The psalmist says that good things happen for the righteous and they can rejoice.

questions.q: What does the psalmist encourage the righteous to do?
questions.a: The psalmist encourages the righteous to be glad in Yahweh and thank him, the one we all know to be holy.

commentary.text: The Lord Jesus reigns in power that cannot be resisted.
His care of his people, and his provision for them.

Verses 1–7 Though many have been made happy in Christ, still there is room. And all have reason to rejoice in Christ's government. There is a depth in his counsels, which we must not pretend to fathom; but still righteousness and judgment are the habitation of his throne. Christ's government, though it might be matter of joy to all, will yet be matter of terror to some; but it is their own fault that it is so. The most resolute and daring opposition will be baffled at the presence of the Lord. And the Lord Jesus will ere long come, and put an end to idol worship of every kind.

The faithful servants of God may well rejoice and be glad, because he is glorified; and whatever tends to his honour, is his people's pleasure. Care is taken for their safety. But something more is meant than their lives. The Lord will preserve the souls of his saints from sin, from apostacy, and despair, under their greatest trials. He will deliver them out of the hands of the wicked one, and preserve them safe to his heavenly kingdom. And those that rejoice in Christ Jesus, and in his exaltation, have fountains of joy prepared for them. Those that sow in tears, shall reap in joy. Gladness is sure to the upright in heart; the joy of the hypocrite is but for a moment. Sinners tremble, but saints rejoice at God's holiness. As he hates sin, yet freely loves the person of the repentant sinner who believes in Christ, he will make a final separation between the person he loves and the sin he hates, and sanctify his people wholly, body, soul, and spirit.
